Please note this recall extends to the entire Butterball family of products, including ground turkey, deli meats, and turkey bacon.”

Buy: ✅ Mahi mahi caught by U.S. fisheries Avoid: 🛑 Imported mahi mahi Mahi are large pelagic fish that mature quickly and have lots of offspring! That makes them less susceptible to overfishing. The main environmental sustainability concerns come from how they’re caught. Fishers use longlines and purse seines to capture these flashy fish, but these methods can have a lot of bycatch if not properly managed. Sticking with U.S.-caught mahi is a good way to ensure your fish comes from strictly regulated fisheries that take measures to reduce bycatch. 🐬Dolphinitely a better choice for the sea! #SeafoodWatch #SustainableSeafood #MahiMahi #Dolphinfish #USCaughtSeafood

For a few hours this summer, streets across Vermont were transformed. The streets that normally divide our neighborhoods with fast traffic suddenly became filled with people. When we close our streets to traffic for a block party, people can safely drag their whole lives out onto the road. They play games and music, eat potluck dinners, chat and meet their neighbors, maybe for the very first time. The most painful part of a block party is announcing that it’s over. Kids drag their feet in the middle of their games, adults cut their conversations short, and the cars start flowing through again. What if it didn’t have to end? Read Jack Evan's full report, Streets Should Be Places, at the link in our bio.

Sun sets before 4:30 PM, which means for most of us, the commute home is in the dark. Drivers, WATCH OUT for people biking, walking, and rolling on the street! Before you pass, slow down. Check for oncoming traffic. As you pass, give at least 4 feet of clearance between your passenger mirror and that person biking, walking, or rolling. Slowing down adds seconds to your drive, and lets them get home safely. Bicyclists, CHARGE YOUR LIGHTS! It can be hard to remember when you ride to work or school in the morning light. By law, and for your own safety, you must have a front white light and rear red light to ride on the street. Walkers, rollers, and bicyclists, BE VISIBLE! We know many drivers are distracted in their cars. Do your best to be seen with gear that reflects, wearing lights, and by taking up space and making yourself known. See more info on road safety for bicyclists, pedestrians, and drivers at the Rules of the Road link in our bio.

posts.c: “Dark Botanica,” on view through January 23 at Burlington City Arts (@btvcityarts), 135 Church St., #BurlingtonVT, “expands the traditional central themes in still-life painting — love, innocence, sensuality, decay to include the polemical. A flower is never only a flower,” writes Marta Pauer-Tursi (@sohochicnyc) in our current issue. “Upon entering the gallery, Marcie Scudder’s oversize installation, “My Mother’s Garden,” captures the viewer’s imagination. The work drapes across the ceiling and against the street facing glass facade of the gallery as a quilt might drape casually across a bed. Made of hundreds of small hexagonal folded papers and photographs of poppies, thistle, myosotis, and stitched together to create a flow of origami flowers, the work references the artist’s mother who left her a garden when she died,” Pauer-Tursi writes. posts.c: Last week we finished up our first adult Learn to Ride class! This free multi week collaboration between Old Spokes Home and Local Motion offered instruction for folks learning to ride for the first time, and for others needing a refresher. This class contributes to Old Spokes Home's overall mission of removing barriers to make bikes work for everyone. It also aligns perfectly with Local Motion's mission of making it safe, accessible, and fun for everyone to bike, walk, and roll in Vermont. The ability to ride a bike, and to ride it safely, opens up opportunities at any age! This class eases students into riding by focusing on balance first. Bikes without cranks and pedals act as adult striders, and as students became more comfortable they work up to bikes with pedals. We'll be offering more FREE adult Learn to Ride classes in the spring!

posts.c: There’s some new faces here so I wanted to reintroduce myself! I’m Jaclyn, and of course you all know my sweet girl, Poppy 🐾 My husband and I got Poppy 3 years ago, and she’s been the center of our world ever since. She’s our fetch obsessed, water loving girl who neverrrr turns down a chance to rough house! This year, Poppy got a brand new title…big sister! 🥹🩵 We recently welcomed our baby boy into the family, and while it took Poppy a little bit to adjust, she’s already starting to love her new role as big sis! She gives her brother kisses, loves to follow us during feedings , night time wakeups and diaper changes. She comes on walks with her brother and is learning how to navigate walking with the stroller! I’m hoping to share more family life with you guys as I navigate motherhood! I’m so happy you’re here, and hope you’ll stick around for more of Poppy’s adventures and life with her little brother. 🤎🐾🩵 #dogs #dogsofinstagram #babyboy #newborn #motherhood

It’s been a great 5 years, and I will not be returning as Market Manager at @shelburnefarmersmarket for the 2027 summer season. HUGE Thanks to the wonderful vendor family I admire so much, and to the wider community that made SFM successful. I am heading into a major surgery, and will be taking time to focus on healing. I will be reframing my work from here, I plan to enjoy slow Saturday mornings for the first time in 5 years, and will be hosting events and working in my own interest going forward. You will see concerts and pop up markets and more from my new events co, @siren.song.events , and the usual herbal body care content from @bearmoonbotanicavt Thanks again, it was a real pleasure to be in community with you all! ❤️ You can find me on socials at @bearmoonbotanicavt @siren.song.events
